description: Use whenever the user asks how a venture fund's terms play out: fund size, management fees and step-downs, carry, investment period, recycling, reserves, deployment pace, and resulting net returns to LPs. Takes fund inputs (start from the defaults and change only what the user specifies) and returns lifetime capital, fees, investable capital and gross/net multiples (result), plus the fund by year (detail): capital calls, fees, investments, distributions, NAV, DPI/RVPI/TVPI, the LP J-curve, IRRs from the dated cash flows, and financial statements whose check lines are zero when they tie out. Optional blocks under features (waterfall terms, fee bases, recycling, LP classes, specific deals, cap-table construction, follow-on timing, a management company) apply only when sent, and each block's schema says how it works. result.grossIRR and result.netIRR are annualized over weighted holding periods; quote detail.irr when the user asks for an IRR from cash flows. For the Excel model, pass format "xlsx_url" and give the user workbook.url. The workbook leaves out the preferred return, clawback and recycling when the fund doesn't use them; set workbookOptions to add them, or to drop the annual detail (Forecast, Annual and Statements, Annual), the Statements sheets or Key reports. Free without an account for a few runs a day; signed in, lifetime free credits or paid access. Fund Economics, a separate $20/year product with 6,000 calculations. If the result contains action_required (not signed in, no purchase, allowance used), relay it to the user with its links and offer to retry. Never skip the calculation silently.

capTable.description: Portfolio construction from a cap table: check size, valuation, follow-on rounds, dilution and outcomes by round. Percentages here are whole numbers (30 = 30%).

deals.description: Build the portfolio from specific deals instead of entry stages and return tiers (and instead of capTable when both are sent). Each deal has its checks, each in a quarter from first close (1-based), and one exit in a quarter, at a multiple of everything invested in the deal (0 is a write-off) or for proceeds in money. Invested capital is the sum of the checks and called capital is solved from it; the fund life runs to the last exit, capped by maxFundLifeYears; each deal comes back as a row of result.tiers. Recycling keeps back the earliest proceeds, up to recycledCapitalPct of committed, only while later checks can use them. Send dealsMix true to mix the methods instead.

multiple.description: Of everything invested in the deal. 0 is a write-off.

proceeds.description: Exit proceeds in money, instead of a multiple.

investments.description: The checks the fund writes into the deal: the initial check, then any follow-ons.

dealsMix.description: With deals: the deals come first, and the capital they leave (committed less fees and expenses, plus recycling, less the checks) is invested through the entry stages and return tiers, or capTable when sent, as it would be without deals. Recycling then goes to the stages, the fund life is the later of the deals' and the stages', and result.tiers lists the deals and then the tiers.

fees.description: Management fee basis: committed, NAV, AUM or a step-down, by year if needed, or the dated LPA schedule.

schedule.description: The fee as an LPA states it, on the dated schedule: each rate from a point in fund years (0 = first close; 5.5 starts halfway through year 6 and cuts the period it lands in), charged on committed capital, invested cost not yet realized, or NAV, with organizational expenses above organizationalExpenseCap offsetting the fee. Runs for feeYears; base, ratePct, yearlyRateSchedule and basesByYear are ignored when it is set.

followOn.description: Follow-on timing for stage-based construction: the average quarters between a first check and its follow-on. The follow-on share comes from each stage's reserveRatio; 0 deploys everything on one schedule.

lpClasses.description: LP classes, each called as the fund needs cash or on its own callSchedule, with optional carry, pref and fee overrides. Each class returns its calls, distributions and net IRR by period, and a datedNetIRR.

callSchedule.description: Call this class on its own schedule instead of as the fund needs cash. pct is a share of the class commitment per fund year (called in the year's first quarter) or per quarter. Whatever the entries leave is called when the fund needs it.

catchup.description: Bring the GP to the new rate on all profit before the tier splits.

irrThreshold.description: Instead of moicThreshold: the band below this tier ends when the LP IRR reaches this rate. With one of these, tiers run in the order given.

moicThreshold.description: The tier starts once LPs reach this multiple.

mgmtCo.description: A management company budget against the fee revenue.

defaultTreatment.description: "retained": proceeds are kept back and never distributed. "deemed": distributed and recontributed, so they count in calledCapital and distributions and are reported as recycledDeemed.

schedule.description: Pin a quarter's recycled amount, skip it with amount 0, or rebook its treatment.

waterfall.description: Preferred return, catch-up and tiered carry. Return of capital covers capital called so far, so carry can be paid on early exits. Rates are decimals (0.08 = 8%). The Excel workbook carries every one of these terms.

basis.description: Whole fund (the default, European) or deal by deal (American): return of capital owes only the capital in deals exited or written off so far, so carry can be paid before the fund returns all capital. The clawback settles on the whole fund.

catchup.description: Bring the GP to the new rate on all profit before the tier splits.

irrThreshold.description: Instead of moicThreshold: the band below this tier ends when the LP IRR reaches this rate. With one of these, tiers run in the order given.

moicThreshold.description: The tier starts once LPs reach this multiple.

catchupMeasure.description: GP catchup: to the carry share of the pref paid (the default), or until the GP holds the carry share of all profit paid. They differ when the GP shares the catchup with LPs.

clawback.description: GP clawback, on by default: at the end the GP is trued back to its carry share of lifetime profit. Reported as gpClawback by period and waterfall.clawback in total.

preferredReturnBase.description: IRR pref: accrue on capital not yet returned plus unpaid pref (the default), or on each contribution from its date whatever comes back.

preferredReturnCompounding.description: IRR pref: compound annually (the default) or simple interest.

firstCloseDate.description: First close (YYYY-MM-DD), for dates on the statements. Defaults to January 1 this year.

format.description: "xlsx_url" adds workbook.url, a 24-hour link to the live Excel workbook with every number a formula back to the inputs. "xlsx" returns it as base64 instead.

fundName.description: Names the workbook and its file.

granularity.description: Periods in detail: "year" (the default), "quarter", or "none" for totals only.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry key; reuse only with identical input.

workbookOptions.description: What the Excel workbook includes: true adds a block, false leaves it out. A feature the fund uses (preferredReturn, clawback, recycling) is always included. Unset, features the fund does not use are left out and every sheet is in. The response echoes the result as workbook.includes.

annualDetail.description: The Forecast, Annual and Statements, Annual sheets: the fund by year, added up from the quarters.

clawback.description: The clawback input, and the clawback test on the Forecast, Quarterly sheet that measures it.

keyReports.description: Six charts of the fund's cash flows, returns and outcomes.

preferredReturn.description: The preferred return and catch-up inputs, and their rows in the waterfall on both forecast sheets.

recycling.description: The recycling inputs, the quarter-by-quarter recycling limits, and the recycled capital rows.

statements.description: Statement of operations, balance sheet and cash flow, by year and by quarter.
